frame_store.description: A stream's recent frames, delivered together at the pace their consumer takes them. Every frame that comes in is kept, in a ring of SLOTS, and the consumer is handed the newest FRAMES whole ones side by side -- channel k the frame k before the newest -- as often as it asks, each with the size and context of the newest. The input never waits for the output: a consumer slower than the source repeats frames of frames, a faster one skips some, neither tears one. A source that reaches a slot being read is never stopped, and `overrun` says so.

BITS.description: One sample of the stream in.

FRAMES.description: Frames delivered together: how far back the consumer reads.

SLOTS.description: Frames kept, FRAMES and the slack: the frames a source may begin, past the newest whole one, while a frame of frames is read.

CTX_BITS.description: The context carried with each frame: whatever rides beside its pixels.

PIXELS.description: The largest frame kept, in samples.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The frames, as their source sends them.

inputs.name: in_frame_width
inputs.description: The width of the frame whose first beat is going in.

inputs.name: in_ctx
inputs.description: Its context, taken with its first beat.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The newest FRAMES frames side by side, newest in the low bits.

outputs.name: out_frame_width
outputs.description: The width of the frames being put out: the newest's.

outputs.name: out_source
outputs.description: Which input frame the frames out are computed at, counted from reset: a repeat shows as the same number.

outputs.name: cold
outputs.description: Fewer than FRAMES frames of one history are whole: nothing goes out.

outputs.name: overrun
outputs.description: Sticky until reset: the source reached a frame being read.

bram.description: The frames in block RAM, one memory a slot, PIXELS samples deep.
